description: Structural/doctrinal CPD priors for Annex C bbn_threat_score. These are cross-assessment modeling constants (how nodes relate to each other), NOT per-assessment analyst inputs. Per-assessment inputs (adversary.capability_prior, adversary.tempo, defensive_posture, geopolitical_trigger_prior) are supplied fresh each run via cpd_config_json and are never read from this file or defaulted -- bbn_threat_score refuses to run if they're missing. IMPORTANT: nearly every value below is an inherited analyst-judgment template default from the original Annex C tutorial, NOT empirically fit to any specific CTI dataset. Review and replace with case-specific sourcing (ATT&CK Groups data, actual SIEM/IDS base rates, CTI reporting) before relying on this for a scored, Commander-ready assessment. Every entry's 'source' field states what it actually is -- do not upgrade these to look more authoritative than they are.

LOW.source: Analyst-judgment template default: confidence smoothing around a LOW tempo assessment (P(actual tempo=low/med/high) given assessed=LOW). Not empirically fit.

MEDIUM.source: Analyst-judgment template default: confidence smoothing around a MEDIUM tempo assessment. Not empirically fit.

HIGH.source: Analyst-judgment template default: confidence smoothing around a HIGH tempo assessment. Not empirically fit.

phishing_given_capability.source: Analyst judgment: nation-state APT groups documented as relying more heavily on spear-phishing for initial access than criminal or hacktivist actors, consistent with general MITRE ATT&CK Groups TTP-frequency patterns. Not fit to a specific CTI dataset for any given assessment -- verify against actor-specific reporting before scored use. Columns are [hacktivist, criminal, nation-state]; rows are [no-phish, phish].

scanning_given_tempo.source: Analyst judgment: higher assessed operational tempo implies proportionally more active reconnaissance/scanning. Not empirically fit -- calibrate against actual SIEM/IDS base rates if available. Columns are [LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH tempo]; rows are [no-scan, scan-detected].

auth_anomaly_root.source: Analyst-judgment credential-reuse/auth-anomaly base rate inherited from the Annex C tutorial template. Treat as a placeholder pending case-specific IAM/SIEM baseline data for the actual system under test.

defensive_posture_floor.source: Modeling-stability floor from the Annex C template's DefensivePosture CPD construction -- prevents a fully-open or fully-hardened posture from producing a degenerate (exactly 0) probability mass. Not an empirical estimate.

defensive_multiplier_floor.source: Annex C template defensive_multiplier() formula: 'max(0.30, 1.0 - (controls_active/total)*0.70)'. A fully-controlled posture still leaves a 30% residual adversary-success floor (defense is never modeled as perfect). Template default, not empirically derived.

defensive_multiplier_scale.source: Annex C template defensive_multiplier() formula: each active control reduces adversary success proportionally, scaled so full control coverage reduces success by 70% (bounded by the floor above). Template default, not empirically derived.

nation_state.source: Analyst judgment: nation-state actors modeled with a 'long-dwell' pattern -- proportionally more probability mass on lateral movement and objective phases -- consistent with general APT tradecraft literature. Not fit to this assessment's specific adversary; treat as a template default. Order: [Recon, InitialAccess, Lateral, Objective].

criminal.source: Analyst judgment template default for criminal-tier actors: faster, shallower kill chains than nation-state. Not empirically fit. Order: [Recon, InitialAccess, Lateral, Objective].

hacktivist.source: Analyst judgment template default for hacktivist-tier actors: mostly recon/opportunistic, rarely reaching Objective. Not empirically fit. Order: [Recon, InitialAccess, Lateral, Objective].

killchain_phase_evidence_delta_phishing.source: Analyst-judgment probability-mass shift applied to KillChainPhase when a phishing attempt is observed: reallocates from Recon to InitialAccess. Magnitude is a template default, not empirically calibrated.

killchain_phase_evidence_delta_scanning.source: Analyst-judgment probability-mass shift when scanning is detected: reallocates from Recon to InitialAccess. Template default, not empirically calibrated.

killchain_phase_evidence_delta_auth_anom.source: Analyst-judgment probability-mass shift when an auth anomaly is observed: reallocates from InitialAccess to Lateral (auth anomalies are treated as a lateral-movement signal). Template default, not empirically calibrated.

iw_effect_phase_base_recon.source: Analyst-judgment ceiling on P(IW effect achieved) when the adversary is only assessed at Recon phase. Template default, not empirically derived.

iw_effect_phase_base_initial_access.source: Analyst-judgment ceiling on P(IW effect achieved) at InitialAccess phase ('early-access ceiling'). Template default.

iw_effect_phase_base_lateral.source: Analyst-judgment ceiling on P(IW effect achieved) at Lateral/Pivot phase. Template default, loosely anchored to KCAG lateral-path traversal rates but not directly computed from them.

iw_effect_objective_convergence_factor.source: Multiplier applied to the Annex B KCAG's max objective-path traversal probability to derive the Objective-phase P(IW effect achieved) ceiling. Template default -- the choice of 2.2 is not empirically derived, only bounded by iw_effect_objective_cap below.

iw_effect_objective_cap.source: Hard ceiling on the Objective-phase P(IW effect achieved) base rate, applied after the convergence-factor multiplication, so the model never asserts near-certainty regardless of KCAG input. Modeling-stability constant.

iw_effect_posture_multiplier_strong.source: Analyst judgment: a strong (fully-controlled) defensive posture reduces P(IW effect) to 25% of its phase-base value. Template default, not empirically derived.

iw_effect_posture_multiplier_moderate.source: Analyst judgment: a moderate defensive posture reduces P(IW effect) to 55% of its phase-base value. Template default, not empirically derived.

iw_effect_geo_multiplier.source: Analyst judgment: an active geopolitical trigger event amplifies P(IW effect) by 45%. Template default, not empirically derived.

iw_effect_geo_cap.source: Hard ceiling applied after the geopolitical multiplier so the model never asserts absolute certainty. Modeling-stability constant.
